page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.3xlarge is a high-clock-speed compute-oriented instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 6149 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 6 physical cores and 12 vCPUs via hyperthreading. Hardware-level support includes AVX and AVX-512 extensions, AES acceleration, and standard bit manipulation instructions. The instance is configured with 24.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage and connects with a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark assessments demonstrate consistent middle-tier multi-threaded processing alongside lower single-core throughput. Synthetic CPU evaluation yields a PassMark CPU score of 11911.02, a multi-core stress-ng throughput of 10809.26, and a Geekbench multi-core result of 5444.0. In contrast, single-thread evaluations reflect architectural aging, as indicated by a single-core Geekbench score of 1087.0 and single-thread gzip compression at 23.32 GB/sec. Large-block memory bandwidth measures 55.98 GB/sec for uncached reads and 38.69 GB/sec for writes, contributing to a lower overall PassMark memory score.

The 1:2 memory ratio and absence of bundled storage require architectural reliance on network-attached storage and cloud network links. Workloads requiring extreme single-thread execution speed or heavy local disk caching will face throughput limits. Conversely, the dedicated core allocation ensures consistent compute availability without contention from shared virtual resources.

Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.3xlarge is suited for moderately parallel compute workloads, CI/CD automated build pipelines, batch data conversion, and distributed worker nodes that benefit from dedicated Intel x86 execution cores.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.3xlarge is a dedicated compute-oriented virtual machine powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 6149 processor on the x86_64 architecture. The system delivers 12 vCPUs across 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, paired with 24.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It includes support for AVX-512 instructions, provides a 2 Gbps baseline network interface, and contains no bundled local storage. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves average multi-core results, reflected in a PassMark CPU score of 11911.02 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 48.86 GB/sec, while single-core metrics fall into lower percentiles. Given its compute-focused density and dedicated CPU scheduling, this instance type fits multi-threaded compilation, batch compute processing, continuous integration routines, and general background application tasks that do not depend on high single-threaded clock speed or local NVMe storage arrays.
